the_correction: This session repeatedly reported '1,443 of 1,950 positions blocked on missing source material, needs a bounded acquisition authorisation'. That framing was wrong in the exact way historical_coverage's own docstring warns about: reading a position count as a work count is what makes a source budget look like the whole remaining cost. 39 metrics share one filing, so the positions collapse.

measured_over_the_full_frame.frame: 10 companies x 39 declared metrics x 5 years = 1950 positions

SOURCE_MISSING_TARGET_ORIGINAL.shape: one 10-K primary document per company-year: seven companies need four prior years each and Marriott needs two, because its 2023 and 2024 originals are already saved. Counted from the manifest above, not by hand - the first version of this sentence said eight companies times four plus two, which is 34.

TARGET_PERIOD_NOT_DISCOVERED.note: not quantified as fetches here, and not therefore zero. Measured since: JPMorgan's three unreachable ordinals are a source need - 57 of its 69 declared submissions shards are not saved - and Paramount's four are a successor-scope question about the predecessor CIK. See acquisition-plan.json classes 2 and 4.

TARGET_PERIOD_METADATA_BLOCKED.correction: this was filed under 'not source problems at all'. That was wrong. Both are JPMorgan, both are HISTORY_SNAPSHOT_CONFLICT, and the cause is that eleven saved shards hold filings outside their currently declared ranges because SEC re-partitioned them. Resolving it needs a refreshed index and refetched shards, which is a source need.

against_the_approved_budget.what_was_written: '30 document fetches against a cumulative SEC allowance of 80. The need fits inside the existing approved budget rather than requiring a new one.'
against_the_approved_budget.wrong_on_authority: the [240, 240, 80] allowance is bound to requirement_id issue_28_v14 and to a 390-coordinate scope, and #47's own text forbids borrowing #28's remainder. The acquisition capability is reusable; its authorisation is not transferable.
against_the_approved_budget.wrong_on_size: 30 was the first blocking reason only. Measured since: 476 event 8-K bodies and up to 40 JPMorgan submissions shards are behind it. The envelope is in the high hundreds, not 30.

the_acquisition_path_exists.constraints_already_bound: the existing SecHttpClient, zero automatic retry, immutable attempts, the same ledger
